_about: Names for Moon Patrol's routines and globals, with the evidence for each.

Provenance: mechanically translated from 6502. Comrec detects it -- 281 `cmc` after cmp/sub, 99% of them straight after a compare. Read as 6502: AL = accumulator, BL and CL = X and Y index registers, no register push/pop, 16-bit as byte pairs with `adc`, every global is a fixed address. See knowledge/14-translated-binaries.md.

Two address bases. File loads .COM at ORG 0x100. Entry stub at file 0 writes a far pointer at run time and does `jmp far [0x140]` to (CS+0x20):0000 -- file offset 0x100 in a new segment addressed from 0. Everything from file 0x100 onward is base-0. Comrec cannot see the target because the pointer is written at run time (Zaxxon and ParaTrooper use `retf`, which comrec autodetects; Moon Patrol does not). build.ps1 passes `--segment 0x100:0 --entry 0x100`.
Copyright string in the file: `Moon Patrol Copyright (C) 1984 Atari, Inc.` at file 0x4E98. The DOS conversion is Atari's, published 1984; the arcade original is Irem, 1982.

DS is set at startup to CS+0x55D paragraphs (`mov bx, cs; sub bx, 0x100; add bx, 0x65D; mov ds, bx`). DS:0x0000 = memory address 0x55D0 in the new segment = file offset 0x56D0. So a bare `[0x81E0]` reads file 0x56D0+0x81E0 = 0xD8B0 -- past the code region (which ends at 0x54C9), inside the 36 KB data tail. `cs:` and bare-DS addresses are two different address spaces.

Routine keys are file offsets, the coordinate comrec's labels use. Global keys are the addresses the program sees. Getting those the wrong way round is the mistake that costs a session, and the only symptom is silence.
This file is being built up. See BRIEF.md for progress and the order the work is worth doing in.

0x002EE: the entry point after the run-time far jmp lands here at file 0x2EE. cli, then writes 0 to port 0xA0 (PC NMI mask register on the 5150/5160, disables NMI), sets SS = CS, computes DS = CS + 0x55D paragraphs (so DS:0 = file 0x56D0, just past the code region), saves DS at ss:0x5C and the original ES at [0x8814], sets SP = 0x1EE (the byte at that offset in the initial stub is data, but the stack grows down from here), calls L_0082E to set up the graphics adapter, unmasks NMI by writing 0x80 to port 0xA0, `sti`, disables the PPI beep by clearing bit 0 of port 0x61, then jumps to L_04ECB (the main menu / title loop)
0x004CB: `pop ds; pop bx; pop ax; iret`. The tail every arm of the keyboard ISR jumps to when it is done. Ax/bx/ds are pushed on entry, ds is set to the game's data segment, then a dispatcher selects the arm from the scancode
0x00505: the ISR arm for scancode 0x1D (LCtrl) or 0x38 (LAlt). Runs the video-setup routine (L_0082E), sets BIOS equipment word bits 4-5 (`or byte [es:0x410], 0x30`), calls int 10h AX=3 (80x25 colour text), then far-jumps to the saved BIOS int 9 handler at [0x8812] -- so this is the Ctrl+Alt+Del exit, chaining to the ROM's own reset path
0x00562: `mov ax, [0x100]; test al, al; ret`. Reads the low byte of the keyboard variable and returns flags. Called by every routine that waits on input
0x00568: loops calling peek_key while the sign flag is not set. Falls into clear_key
0x0056D: `and byte [0x100], 0x7F; ret`. Clears the 'key ready' top bit that the ISR sets. Called after a wait so the next peek starts clean
0x00573: sets up 320x200 4-colour CGA. Zeroes [0x8818] (in-game flag), sets ES = 0 to reach the BIOS data area, clears equipment bits 4-5 and sets bit 5 (color adapter present), int 10h AX=4 (CGA mode 4), records the mode in [0x8819] = 4, then does int 10h AH=0Bh BH=1 to set palette 1 (cyan/magenta/white) and int 10h AH=0Bh BH=0 to set background 0. Falls into L_0085D
0x005A3: sets SP = 0x1EE, zeroes [0x8818] (in-game) and ss:0x5A (frame counter) and [0x8819] (mode marker), runs int 10h (mode) and L_0085D, then falls into the menu render loop at L_005B7
0x005B7: the menu render entry -- prints the string at DS:0x81E0 (`Game Options`) and clears the key latch. Falls into L_005C0
0x005C0: the menu poll loop -- prints the demo copy at DS:0x84B7 once every 500 timer ticks, then walks a per-key table looking for a matching scancode and dispatching. Two special scancodes fall through to sub-menus at L_0060A (2D = 'Z', jumps into player-select) and L_0064B (2E = 'C', jumps into course-config)
0x00645: two instructions: `call print_string; jmp wait_key_up`. The universal 'show this line and hold until the player releases the key' pattern the menu uses for every submenu title and confirmation
0x0064B: walks a (scancode, action) pair table at DS:0x88A9 -- pairs terminated by an 0xFFFF entry. For each pair, scans 0x53 bytes at DS:0x8856 for the matching scancode, then writes the action byte into whatever cell the action's second word points at. This is the input remap step used by the [K]/[J] menu
0x0066D: the accept branch of scancode_dispatch: prints DS:0x84D9 (the 'PRESS KEY' prompt), reads a scancode via peek_key/wait_key_up chain, swaps it into the two mirrored key-map cells at [si - 0x77AB] and [di - 0x77AB], updates the display cells at [0x8712], [0x872B], [0x8742], flips [0x8853], and jumps back to scancode_dispatch to install the next binding
0x006BF: the joystick-calibration/read dispatcher. Sets [0x82B1] = 0xF0, then calls read_joystick_raw three times with three different bases (0x8832, 0x8836, 0x883A) -- min-x, max-x, min-y or similar -- with the caller's function pointer invoked between reads (`call ax`/`call bx`). Ends by scaling the readings into `[si - 0x77DE]` scale factors used by later reads
0x0073F: reads the joystick if input mode is joystick ([0x8853] == 1), applies the min/max calibration written by run_calibrate_or_read, and returns the scaled axes. Uses port 0x201 via read_joystick_raw and compares against the per-axis min/max cells at [bx - 0x77E2] and [bx - 0x77CA]
0x00789: returns the joystick position -- from port 0x201 if input mode is joystick ([0x8853] == 1), otherwise from the cached values at [0x881A]/[0x881C] that the last real read left there. Every game-loop input path funnels through here
0x007AB: raw poll of the IBM PC game port at 0x201. cli, arm the one-shots by writing to the port, then a 256-iteration loop reading `in al, dx` and testing each of the four RC-timed bits; each axis returns the count at which its bit dropped. The write to [0x883E] = 0xFF marks the readings as valid
0x0088D: prints a string from DS:SI straight into CGA text-mode video RAM. Sets ES = 0xB800, `lodsb`, `cmp al, 0xff` -- the terminator is 0xFF. For each character, computes `row * 80 * 2 + col * 2 + 4` (`ah = 0x50; mul ah; add ax, 4`) and writes attribute + char into `[es:ax]`. Every menu, prompt, score and end-of-game string funnels through here
0x0082E: the interrupt vector installer/restorer used by startup and by reset_and_reboot. ES = 0, then walks a table pointed to by BP with (offset, seg, offset-of-old) triples: reads the table's entry, if the seg field is 0 the CS-relative install path takes over, otherwise it restores the saved vector. Same routine drives install and teardown -- the direction is encoded in the table
0x0085D: writes to the CGA CRTC via port 0x3D4 (index/data pair) using the scroll offset in [0x8817]. Sets registers 0x0E (cursor-hi = 0xFF, effectively hiding the cursor) and 0x03 (h-sync width = 0x0A), then a MA-lookup pair driven by [0x8817]. This is the raster-timed split that lets the score line stay on top while the game field scrolls below
0x00A6D: cl = 2, then loops writing `al` (=0) to `[si + 0xE8]` and `[si + 0xEB]` for si = 2, 1, 0 -- clears three pairs of state bytes at 0x0E8/0x0EB, 0x0E9/0x0EC, 0x0EA/0x0ED. Same shape as the 'zero this small array' the game uses everywhere at round boundaries
0x00A82: queues two notes into the L_05134 sound engine: al = 1, cl = [0x59] | [0x216], bl = [0x5A]; then al = 0, cl = [0x61] | [0x216], bl = [0x62]. The `| [0x216]` OR is a volume/priority mask the sound flag sets. Pair pattern (voice 1 then voice 0) appears throughout the sound path
0x00ACA: same shape as queue_sound_pair_L134 but goes to the L_05115 engine and uses cells [0x57], [0x58], [0x5B]. Two engines, two note tables -- probably the two square-wave voices the 8253/PIT can drive on channel 2
0x00CA0: if [0x225] != 0 (6502-idiom `mov al, X; inc al; dec al; jne` sets Z from AL like LDA): falls into the [0x100] check at L_00CAC, otherwise jumps to L_00D11. Reads the keyboard state to decide whether to advance a script
0x011E0: cl = 2 loop over the three bullet slots. For each slot: if `[si + 0xE8] == 0` (6502-idiom zero check), jump to L_011F1 (idle branch), otherwise L_011F8 (active branch). Iterates the three-slot bullet array clear_bullet_slots initialised
0x022EE: the inline-script interpreter, called 25+ times. `pop word [5]; dec word [5]` pops the return address into the 16-bit cell at [5..6] -- the interpreter's PC -- and backs it up by one so the first `inc byte [5]` at L_022FE walks it forward one byte. Then stores CL and BL into [3] and [4] as script arguments. Every caller of this is `call script_run; db opcodes...` -- the routine reads opcodes out of the caller's own code stream and never returns to the byte after the call. This is the dominant control-flow shape of the whole game
0x04ECB: the target of startup's final `jmp`. Zeroes [0x231], [0x230], [0x22F] (probably player/round/level counters), calls enter_cga_graphics with ax=0, then renders the title screen: loads si from the pointer at [0x2F84] and calls L_054B2 (draws the title art), then loads si from [0x2F86] and calls the OR-blit at L_053F9 at (cx=0x15, dx=0xB9). Where the menu proper takes over
0x009C3: zeroes the two ammo cells [0x222] and [0x22A], then falls into reset_round_state
0x009CD: the round-init clear: writes [0x6E] = 0x22, [0x41] = [0x43] = 0x15, zeroes twelve state cells around [0x28..0x29] and [0xBB..0xC0], then continues with more state bytes -- the shape of a per-wave BSS clear. Called after ammo reset when a new round starts
0x020DB: calls L_05172 (a draw), then copies [0x43] into [0x41] and increments [0x43]; if the new [0x43] hits 0x8D it wraps back to 0. The 0x8D matches the code-region horizontal cell count -- this is the terrain scroll pointer, and its wrap is where the horizon loops
0x021E8: hard-codes cx = 0x18 (24 columns) into [0xA6] and dx = 0x0F (15 rows) into [0xA7], then calls the sprite-draw pair for the score/status bar using [0x7E] (score digit) and [0x7D] (fuel or similar)
0x02249: the BCD score add. `add al, [0x7A]; daa; mov [0x7A], al` -- classic BCD accumulator using DAA. AL comes from the score-value argument, [0x7A] is the ones digit; the daa preserves the packed-BCD invariant so `[0x7A]` never leaves 0..99. The full 8-digit score lives in [0x7A..0x81]
0x032E0: 6502-style bit permutation. Reads [0x20] and rotates five bits into AL through carry, then rotates carry into AH, XORs back with [0x20]. This is the 6502 shape for a shape-table byte unpack -- the same idiom the Applesoft turtle-graphics interpreter used, carried across by the translator (see knowledge/14-translated-binaries.md)
0x04CAE: 6502 subtract-with-cmc test on [0x28] vs [0xAF]. If >=, add 7 to al and dec [0x29]; otherwise fall through. Reads the object's row and either advances the vertical counter or moves to the next slot
0x04F70: single `ret`. One of three empty callback slots at 0x4F70/71/72 the game overrides with sound or draw handlers -- comrec sees only the initial nop-return that the sound-on/off toggle patches back to when muted
0x04F73: one-instruction `jmp show_menu_and_wait`, so the caller can push a return address the menu unwinds by resetting SP
0x04F76: nested `dec al; nop; jne` loop -- inner loop runs 256 times per outer, outer runs AL times, so AL squared * ~4 cycles. The game's short pause between menu clicks and sound events
0x04F83: `lahf; and byte [0x100], 0x7f; sahf; ret`. Same as clear_key but preserves flags around the mask -- called from arithmetic sequences that need the surrounding carry to survive
0x04F8B: `lahf; in al, 0x61; xor al, [0x8852]; and al, [0x896E]; out 0x61, al; sahf; ret`. The 1-bit PC speaker bit-bang. [0x8852] is the toggle mask (usually 0x02, the speaker output bit), [0x896E] is the sound-on gate (0xFF when sound on, 0xFD or so when muted so the XOR is discarded). Flags preserved so the caller's timing loop keeps its counter
0x04F9A: reads the calibrated joystick and returns bit 7 = fire, bit 0 = left/right. `rcr ch, 1` on entry and `rcl ch, 1` on exit rotate a status bit into and out of a caller's register. Wraps poll_joystick_scaled
0x04FB4: like poll_joystick_x_bit but wraps read_joystick_or_cache and ands with ah (the fire-button mask) then xors 0x80 to invert the sense -- the game's 'is the button pressed' predicate
0x04FC6: atomic clear-then-draw guarded by a one-byte semaphore at [0x896D]: `inc byte [0x896D]; je skip; dec [0x896D]; ...`. The body sets ES = 0xB800 and does `rep stosb cx=0x4000` -- clears all 16 KB of CGA memory -- then loads si from [0x2F80] and draws through L_053F9. Used for full screen transitions
0x050D7: one of a 2x2 family (0x50D7/0x50F6/0x5115/0x5134) whose only differences are (a) which sprite table they index and (b) which blit routine they call. Common shape: `cbw; shl ax,1; xchg si,ax; mov si,[si+table]; mov al,7; imul byte [0x39]; add cx,ax; call blit; clear bx/cx/dx; ret`. Al is the sprite id, cx is the row (multiplied by 7 * [0x39] scale), bl is the column. This one reads table 0x1242 and calls L_053F9, the XOR blit -- so it erases (undraws) a sprite from atlas B
0x050F6: table 0x1242, blit L_05432 (OR-copy). Draws a sprite from atlas B. Same shape as erase_sprite_B
0x05115: table 0x1210, blit L_053F9. Erases a sprite from atlas A
0x05134: table 0x1210, blit L_05432. Draws a sprite from atlas A
0x05153: table 0x1210, blit L_05432, but scales by [0x33] instead of [0x39]. Used where a different sprite class has its own y-stride -- probably the fixed HUD row that never scrolls
0x00513: the ISR arm reached by falling through reset_and_reboot when the tested scancode was not Ctrl or Alt but a key that repeats. Pushes [0x100], forces the latch to 0x7F, zeroes ss:0x5A, then loops peek_key at L_0053C with a 0xCCC-tick timeout -- the auto-repeat hold that the [S]ound and joystick-configure menus rely on
0x008CF: trampoline: `mov cl, 8; mov bl, 0x4e; call script_run`. Runs a fixed-parameter script for one of the standard events. The junk `add [bx+si], ah` decoding after the call is the inline opcode stream script_run reads, not real instructions
0x008F3: `mov cl, 0; mov sp, 0x1EE; call on_key_225` -- resets the stack to the fixed 0x1EE top and then runs the input-driven advance. Called from the main round loop as the single entry that both restores the stack after a game-loop unwind and processes input
0x00C9A: one instruction: `jmp L_04EDA` -- into main_menu_entry after its initial state clear, so callers that already zeroed those cells skip the redundant clears
0x00E2B: if [0x13] == 0 (6502 idiom): sets [0x10] = 0xFC. Otherwise returns. First of three state-transitions guarded on [0x13] -- the trio at 0xE2B/0xE4B/0xE6B sets [0x10] to 0xFC, 4 and 0 respectively, so [0x10] is a signed velocity component driven from the state byte [0x13]. Guessed role: horizontal speed of the moon buggy in three states (accel left / accel right / idle)
0x00E4B: if [0x13] == 0: sets [0x10] = 4. See check_var13_set_10_FC for the family shape
0x00E6B: if [0x13] == 0: sets [0x10] = 0 and [0x15] = 0. The idle / stop branch of the trio
0x00F3F: if [0x1A] == 0: sets [0x9D] = 0, then reads [0x57] and stores it -- resets the horizontal buggy X to the value the wave chose. Companion to L_00E family for vertical vs horizontal state
0x00FF3: if [0x1A] != 0: jump to L_010BC; else checks [0x1C] for further branching. A two-level dispatch on the same pair of state cells check_var1A_reset_9D_57 initialises
0x01164: reads the drift value at [0x14] out of the lane position [0x58], writes it back, then adds 8 to that new value and stores it as the following three lane positions [0x5C], [0x5E], [0x60]. The 8-apart spacing means these are four lanes stepped by a fixed pitch
0x011B1: `mov al, [0x96]; sub al, [0xAF]; cmc; mov [0x96], al; jae L_011C1`. Subtracts [0xAF] from [0x96] with the 6502 carry-invert convention and writes back. Then bumps [0xDD] on the >= branch. Position update -- probably obstacle-Y decrement each frame, with the branch guarding underflow
0x011DF: single `ret` -- a callback slot the game overrides at run time
0x0124B: `mov [0x50], cl; sub al, 0xF; cmc; mov cl, al; mov si, cx; mov al, [si+0xDFE]; push ax; mov al, [si+0xE02]; push ax` -- indexes two parallel four-entry tables at DS:0xDFE and DS:0xE02 by (al - 0xF), pushes both values. Used where the caller needs a pair of related values from a table
0x0127A: `cmp al, 0xC; cmc; jb L_01282; jmp L_012EA`. Small dispatcher: al < 0xC one branch, else other. AL comes from the state cell [0xE0] visible at L_01282
0x01318: trampoline: `mov cl, 7; mov bl, 0x35; call script_run`. See script_run_cl8_bl4E
0x01382: reads the current script pointer at word [0x75], grabs one byte from it into [0x54], then hard-codes [0x55] = 0xE0 and [0x56] = 0xB (probably screen-column and lane-count constants for the entity this script drives)
0x01474: copies the wave's starting X and Y from [0x44]/[0x45] into [0x99]/[0x9A], clears [0x97], sets [0x96] = 0x18. The vertical position starts at 24 lines down from the top, and [0x97] is the countdown that ticks it toward zero
0x014AB: if [0x97] == 0 (6502 idiom): jump to L_014BA; else L_0150C. The countdown terminated -- L_014BA is the action, L_0150C the noop
0x0150D: cl = 3 for-each loop over four slots at DS:[si+0x90A]. For each: if slot's first byte is zero, skip; else run L_01527 (the collision/hit action). One of the family of `mov cl, 3` iterators over four-entry object arrays
0x01603: cl = 3 iterator over the same four slots at DS:[si+0x90A] as for_each_slot_90A_hit, but the branch is L_0161B -- the per-frame step, not the hit test
0x01667: cl = 3 iterator over four slots at DS:[si+0x82B] (a different array). Zero => L_01678 (idle), non-zero => L_016AC. Probably rockets or enemy shots
0x017A4: collision test: computes ([0xAF] >> 1) - 1 into [0x0], then subtracts that from [0x46] with 6502 carry-invert. Half of [0xAF] is the sprite's own vertical extent halved -- an axis test between the moon buggy's [0x46] and an obstacle's [0xAF]
0x01AE8: cl = 3 iterator over the four slots at DS:[si+0x82B], zero-slot branch. Companion to for_each_slot_82B_step -- likely the hit test the step routine skips
0x01C6F: cl = 3 iterator over four slots at DS:[si+0x8BE]. Non-zero => L_01C83 (advance); reset by writing al into [0xB0] first
0x01D08: cl = 3 iterator over the same four slots at DS:[si+0x8BE] as for_each_slot_8BE_zeroing but the zero branch takes L_01D19. Companion to it
0x01F17: cl = 0 iterator (single-shot) over slot at DS:[si+0x8F3]. Zero-branch pattern -- similar to the 0x8BE family but a different array
0x02100: sets scratch [0] = 0xF, then reads [0x22A] and dispatches on its zero-state. Called from the level-transition path
0x02140: sets [0xA6] = 6 and [0xA7] = 6 (screen position), then reads [0x22F] (which player is scoring). The single-player score sprite draw at column 6 row 6
0x02169: compares the active player index at [0x22F] with the round-owner at [0x7C]. 6502 cmp-cmc convention. Two branches: match => L_02176, mismatch => L_0217E
0x021BF: same shape as place_score_at_6_6 but at [0xA6] = 0x1A, [0xA7] = 0x73 -- the fuel/lives sprite draw. Reads [0x21A]
0x02232: shifts AL right by four (four `shr al, 1` because the translator emits shifts one bit at a time -- a 6502 has no multi-bit shift), so the high nibble becomes the digit index, then draws it. The score display's tens-digit path
0x022CD: adds an offset from [0x21C] and the caller's cl argument to the score digit. Mid-level score-add helper
0x023A3: reads column/row from [0xA6]/[0xA7], adds 0x2F to al (the '0' sprite offset), calls the blit at L_050BA, then increments [0xA6] -- advance to the next column. The score-digit stamp used in a loop
0x023B5: compares [0x78] with 4. Two branches. [0x78] is a mode selector -- probably the wave-count 0..4 that keeps recycling
0x027EE: cl = 3 iterator over [si + 0x82B], a third arm of the same array (companions: 0x1667/0x1AE8)
0x02A93: cl = 3 iterator over [si + 0x82B]. Fourth arm; the four routines together are draw, undraw, step and hit for the same object class
0x02B49: reads sprite id from [0x78], sets cl = 0x19, bl = 6, calls the L_050BA blit and returns. Fixed-position render for a HUD element
0x02B54: cl = 3 iterator over [si + 0x8BE]. Third companion to for_each_slot_8BE_zeroing/action
0x02C97: cl = 3 iterator over [si + 0x8F3]. Companion to L_02EC1 and L_045FB
0x02FBC: sets [si + 0x84B] = 0x1E and [si + 0x83B] = 0x14 for the slot in cx. Object spawn -- 0x1E and 0x14 are its starting Y and X, and 0x84B/0x83B are per-slot arrays 16 bytes apart
0x03366: zeroes [0x6E] and calls L_05213 (compute screen ptr) and L_0500D (clear video pages). One of the two most-central resets, called from every 'go back to menu' path
0x034D4: sets [0x21D] = 1 and reads [0x216]. Sets the sound-on latch
0x03590: the full-reset sequence: clear_key_flags_preserved, hard_reset_state, L_05044 (a second page clear), then set [0x21D] = 1. Called between rounds
0x03E27: reads DS:[si + 0xF0A] into al, then repeatedly adds byte [6] while carry not set. The 6502 `LDA / ADC` inner loop the translator emits for a wrap-based counter
0x03E3B: `mov [0] = al; mov [1] = cl; mov al, 0; mov cl, 8; loop`. Sets up an 8-iteration bit-shift loop -- the shape the translator emits for a byte-wide serial output (probably the tune player's per-sample step)
0x03E99: `mov [3] = al; mov cl, 0x1E; loop`. A 30-step iteration -- exactly one CGA vertical retrace tick's worth of accumulation at 60 Hz
0x03EB2: sets [6] = 1 and cl = 0xD2. Prime for a counted operation of 210 steps
0x03EC1: if [0xA0] == 0: L_03ECD; else L_03F02. Same 6502 zero-check idiom
0x03FB2: calls L_051E1 (some setup), then subtracts [0xAF] from [0xD8] with 6502 cmc. Collision test between the buggy at [0xD8] and an obstacle's height at [0xAF]
0x03FCC: if [0x216] == 0: L_03FD8; else L_04002. Sound-flag gate -- [0x216] is the sound-on toggle
0x040B6: pushes [0x22A], then sets [0x235] = 1 and zeroes a series of state cells. Enter a scoped state that will be popped later
0x040E3: sets [0x21D] = 1, then checks [0x235] == 0. Companion to save_var22A_set_235 -- the tear-down
0x04164: cl = 3 iterator over [si + 0x8BE]. Yet another arm of the 8BE family
0x042DC: if [0x22A] == 0: L_042E8; else L_04347. Zero-state check for the queue at [0x22A]
0x045E1: reads [0x218], subtracts 1 with 6502 cmc, pushes result, sets al = 0x25. Read a countdown and act on its previous value
0x047D1: if [0xBD] == 0: L_047DD; else L_047DE. State check
0x04814: if [0xC0] == 0: L_04820; else L_04821. State check
0x048CC: if [0xBB] != 0: L_048D7; else L_048CB. State check
0x04969: if [0xBB] == 0: L_04975; else L_04976. Companion to check_var_BB_nonzero for the opposite branch
0x04D70: trampoline: `mov si, 0xB75; jmp L_04D7D`. Sound effect data at DS:0xB75 -- probably one of the alarm/explosion tones
0x04D75: trampoline: `mov si, 0xBBC; jmp L_04D7D`. Sound effect data at DS:0xBBC
0x04D7A: trampoline: `mov si, 0xDA7; jmp L_04D7D`. Sound effect data at DS:0xDA7
0x04D7D: the shared body of the sound-effect trampolines -- the caller loads SI with a data pointer, this walks it
0x0500D: bp = 0x48 loop reading segment values from DS:[bp + 0x53C9] and doing `xor al; mov cx, 0x46; ...` -- clears cx*4 bytes at each page. DS:0x53C9 is the scanline pointer table; walking bp from 0x48 downward walks through page pointers

the 21,705-byte code region 0x0000..0x54C9 (88.3% recovered as instructions;
the remaining ~11.7% is tables and small in-line data comrec left as db) and
the 36,601-byte data tail 0x54C9..0xE302 (sprite atlases, tables, strings, sound
data and game scripts). The spans below partition the whole file; each names
what the extent is for, with evidence.
Spans of pure code inside the code region are not enumerated individually --
the region map at recovered/moon-patrol.map has 90+ code runs interleaved with

them as db to preserve the original bytes), not data proper.

_note: The bracketed constants below are indexed forms -- `[si + BASE]` or
`[bx + BASE]` -- that never appear as a lone `[BASE]` in the code. Each
names the head of an array that the game walks by loading an index into
the base register, so the address in the entry is the *start* of an
array or struct rather than a single scalar. They are kept here rather
than in globals because annotate.py's audit distinguishes the two forms.
Most of the low-address (0x0002A..0x0300) and 0x08XX-0x09XX bases are
four-slot per-object arrays that the `mov cl, 3; ...` iterators sweep --
the games' equivalent of a struct-of-arrays for the four enemy/obstacle/
bullet slots. The 4-byte-aligned stride from 0x0823 through 0x08FB is
the most visible signature of this layout: each 4-byte group is one
field, and there are 30-plus fields per slot. The 0x0DEA..0x0E06 range
is a smaller two-array pair L_0124B indexes into for its parallel
lookups. The high ones (0x740F..0x7896) are the sound engine's per-voice
tables walked through di/si by play_sound_effect.
